title: Assisted living, group home, or residential facility death: home-like room under policy and staffing limits

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source setting-axis synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no public rendering, no clinical/legal/operational authority.
limitations: Public sources support vocabulary, setting gates, search routing, and review needs only.
Setting records must not be rendered as clinical, legal, emergency, funeral, investigative, ritual, or operational advice.
Individual experience depends on local care systems, law, facility policy, culture, family structure, safety, resources, and the person’s wishes.
Public-health or institutional data cannot supply bedside texture or replace consented witness testimony.

moment.plain_scene: The room may contain personal furniture and photographs, but medication rules, visiting policies, staffing levels, and transfer decisions may belong to a facility.

content_layers.observation_text: The room may contain personal furniture and photographs, but medication rules, visiting policies, staffing levels, and transfer decisions may belong to a facility.
content_layers.source_synthesis: This setting is neither simply home nor hospital; the record tracks the split between personal belonging and institutional policy.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This setting-axis record exists to prevent the archive from treating place as background. It records how setting controls witnesses, vocabulary, risk, privacy, body access, and next-step authority while remaining quarantined.

what_this_is_not: not a prediction of time left
not proof that any setting is safe or unsafe for every person
uncertainties: The current record is a source-bound scaffold, not a lived scene.
More consented testimony is needed from the relevant witness roles before public rendering.
Local law, facility policy, and culture may change what can be said or done in this setting.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface may orient a reader to why this place feels different from another death room. It must not give step-by-step instructions, legal guidance, emergency decisions, or claims about what should happen next.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Practitioner surfaces should collect setting, who had access, who controlled the body or room, who was absent, which words were used, what was hidden by policy, and what handoff came next.
language_notes: Name the setting before generalizing from it.
Do not call a death good or bad solely because of place.
Do not erase custody, homelessness, poverty, race, disability, language, or institutional control when they shaped access to the room.
Use public-health and institutional terms only as terms, not as complete accounts of what happened.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the setting axis. Requires setting-specific professional review, equity/trauma review, plain-language review, and lived-witness testing before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is not medical advice. It does not diagnose, predict, verify death, recommend treatment, explain emergency action, or replace local care teams.
safety.legal_boundary: This record is not legal advice. Verification, certification, notification, investigation, custody, body release, funeral, cremation, burial, and reporting rules are jurisdiction-specific.

open_review_questions: Which witness roles are missing from this record?
What would be unsafe if a lay reader treated this as a next-step guide?
What does this setting hide or make visible?
What local-law or policy boundaries must be named before public rendering?
